profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point in Siena, Italy, tagged telecom=data_center, is named E. D. Accounting Siena. The word "Accounting" in the business name plainly identifies this as an accounting or bookkeeping practice serving local clients, not a data center or IT hosting business. Accounting firms maintain their own office computing and, in many cases, client financial-record servers, but that is a fundamentally different function from a commercial colocation or cloud data center. The telecom=data_center tag on this point is best explained as a mapping error applied to the firm's own small server room or network closet, and this entry records that determination plainly rather than inventing data-center specifications for an accounting office.

reading.body:
A point tagged as a data center in Siena, Italy is an accounting firm, not compute infrastructure. The name E. D. Accounting Siena identifies a bookkeeping practice, and the tag most plausibly reflects the firm's own server closet.

The record carries no capacity figure, no operator, and no website. Its only listed source is an OpenStreetMap tagging review. That is the whole of what is known here, and it is enough to classify the entry as a mapping error rather than a facility.

This matters for AI because data-center counts drawn from open mapping data will overstate capacity if office server rooms are counted alongside commercial colocation. One mislabeled accounting office does not move a national total. It does show the error mode: a tag applied to a small room, then inherited by any dataset that trusts the tag.

What the data does not say is how many similar points exist, in Italy or elsewhere. It covers one node, at one address, with one determination. The nearest airport is six miles away, which says nothing about the site's suitability, and the suitability field is empty.
